text:
Karel Vejmelka was one of the league's better workhorses the last two seasons, with Evolving-Hockey crediting him with more than 20 goals saved above expected in each. This season he's at .868 and 6.1 goals worse than expected over 15 starts, and Utah's skid has gone through his crease.

The detail is interesting. He's been fine on the hard ones, .722 on high-danger shots against a league .685, but he's let in too many easy goals: .940 on low-danger shots against a league .963. That's a goalie who's not giving his team the routine saves, and it's why the Mammoth have dropped games despite controlling 57% of the five-on-five chances. He's 6-6-2, and 2.3 goals worse than expected over his last five starts.

Our talent range expects him to recover toward .885, which is closer to who he's been. Utah needs that recovery sooner rather than later. Watch the low-danger goals first. When those stop, the rest of his numbers should follow.
